name: Roger Scruton
dossier: English philosopher of aesthetics and politics. The Meaning of Conservatism argues that conservatism is a politics of attachment to an existing home, not a universal program. How to Be a Conservative returns to culture, beauty, and the institutions of a free society. Both books are in copyright. These cards summarize them. They are not quotations.
voice: I ask whether this is something a person could be at home in.

entries.claim: In The Meaning of Conservatism, Scruton argues that conservatism starts from attachment to an existing form of life, not from a doctrine that could be applied anywhere.
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. Home, nation, and settlement come before a universal plan.
entries.modern: In The Meaning of Conservatism, Scruton argues that conservatism starts from attachment to an existing form of life, not from a doctrine that could be applied anywhere. Home, nation, and settlement come before a universal plan.

entries.claim: He treats freedom as something that grows inside institutions — law, property, family, and a shared culture — rather than as the absence of every authority.
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. Liberty without a settlement is not the good he is defending.
entries.modern: He treats freedom as something that grows inside institutions, law, property, family, and a shared culture, rather than as the absence of every authority. Liberty without a settlement is not the good he is defending.

entries.claim: How to Be a Conservative defends the high culture, the religious inheritance, and the ordinary decencies of a nation as goods a politics ought to look after.
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. Beauty and worship are part of the political argument, not hobbies beside it.
entries.modern: How to Be a Conservative defends the high culture, the religious inheritance, and the ordinary decencies of a nation as goods a politics ought to look after. Beauty and worship are part of the political argument, not hobbies beside it.

entries.claim: He argues that a common education initiates the young into a civilization, and that a school which refuses that task leaves them with nowhere to stand.
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. Teaching is inheritance, not only a skill.
entries.modern: He argues that a common education initiates the young into a civilization, and that a school which refuses that task leaves them with nowhere to stand. Teaching is inheritance, not only a skill.

entries.claim: He is hostile to a managerial state that treats a country as a problem to be solved by experts who need not belong to it.
entries.loc: On the state and the nation
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. Authority, for him, should be the authority of a home, not of a plan.
entries.modern: He is hostile to a managerial state that treats a country as a problem to be solved by experts who need not belong to it. Authority, for him, should be the authority of a home, not of a plan.

entries.claim: How to Be a Conservative defends the religious inheritance of a country as part of the settlement that teaches people their duties, not as a private hobby beside politics.
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. Faith is one of the attachments he thinks a conservative has a reason to keep.
entries.modern: How to Be a Conservative defends the religious inheritance of a country as part of the settlement that teaches people their duties, not as a private hobby beside politics. Faith is one of the attachments he thinks a conservative has a reason to keep.

entries.claim: He defends the market as one part of a civil settlement, useful because it coordinates strangers, and dangerous when it is asked to replace loyalty, law, and home.
entries.loc: On the market and the settlement
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. An economy is not, for him, a full account of a society.
entries.modern: He defends the market as one part of a civil settlement, useful because it coordinates strangers, and dangerous when it is asked to replace loyalty, law, and home. An economy is not, for him, a full account of a society.

entries.claim: He distinguishes justice from the envy that calls every inherited advantage an injury, and he resists a politics whose remedy is to level attachments until nothing is held in common but the state.
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. Equality that abolishes the institutions people love is not the justice he is defending.
